featureRef: 28.2 Publishing and removing the online inquiry form
name: Put the admission inquiry form on the website, and take it down when the school is not taking inquiries
priorityReason: An inquiry form left up when the school has no places collects applications it cannot answer.

goal.capability: to control whether the inquiry form is on the school website
goal.outcome: families can apply when the school is taking inquiries, and are told plainly when it is not

secondaryActors.involvement: Publishes or removes the form where they hold the permission instead.

externalActors.involvement: Carries the form, or the notice that inquiries are closed. Holds no login.

additional.description: A prospective family submits the published form, and the submission enters the system as an online inquiry.

preconditions.condition: The Super Admin has granted the acting user the right to publish to the website (BR-1).
The inquiry form and its fields exist. They are specified elsewhere, not here (BR-2).
The school website is reachable. Where it is not, nothing changes and that is reported.

postConditions: The inquiry form is either on the site or off it, and which was a deliberate act by somebody holding the permission.
While it is up, a prospective family could complete it and their submission entered the system as an online inquiry.
While it is down, the page said plainly that inquiries are closed rather than showing nothing or a broken form.
Publishing and removing were both logged with who did it and when.
Nothing about the form's fields or what happens to a submission was decided here. Those belong to the inquiry use case.
A submission already made was unaffected by the form being taken down afterwards.

businessRules.rule: The right to publish or remove the form is the same website permission the Super Admin grants. A member of staff or the School Admin can hold it.
This use case controls only whether the form is on the site. The form's fields and what happens to a submission are specified in the inquiry use case, and nothing about either is decided here.
A prospective family completes the published form and their submission enters the system as an online inquiry. They hold no login and see nothing else of the school's system.
When the form is removed, the page says plainly that inquiries are closed. A page showing nothing, or a form that fails on submission, tells a family nothing and loses them.
Publishing and removing are both logged with who did it and when. A school asked why it received no inquiries in March must be able to see that the form was down.
A submission already made is unaffected by the form being taken down afterwards. An inquiry received is an inquiry that must still be answered.
Where the website cannot be reached, nothing changes and it is reported rather than the form appearing to have been published or removed.
The form is up or it is down. There is no partial state, no scheduling and no per-class control, because a family either can apply or cannot.

transitions.condition: Removed, and the page says inquiries are closed (BR-4).

departures.requirement: There is no partial state, no scheduling and no per-class control. A family either can apply or cannot.
With the form down the page states plainly that inquiries are closed. It never shows nothing, and never shows a form that fails on submission.
Taking the form down affects no submission already made.
A publish or removal that could not reach the website is reported rather than appearing to have taken effect.
The form's state history is retained 7 years, since it explains why inquiries were or were not received in a period.

openQuestions.assumption: Not modelled. The page tells them to come back.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
